2607.15439.title: Do Coding Agents Need Executable World Models, Simplification, and Verification to Solve ARC-AGI-3?
2607.15439.paper_summary: Our previous ARC-AGI-3 agent bundled executable world modeling, scheduled simplification, and exact replay verification, leaving unclear which idea accounted for its performance. We address this attribution question with four nested Codex-based agents: a textual baseline; a flexible-interface executable world model without replay verification; the same executable model with scheduled simplification; and a fixed-interface verification treatment that retains simplification and requires exact reproduction of recorded observations. The main study evaluates all four agents with gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5 at high and xhigh reasoning effort on the public ARC-AGI-3 games. Exploratory follow-ups evaluate the textual and verification variants with gpt-5.6-sol at xhigh and max. The most robust result is that every agent variant improves with a stronger model and with greater reasoning effort. Within each model-effort setting, differences among variants are smaller than anticipated, while the effects of individual components vary across settings. Requiring a persistent executable deliverable is not universally beneficial: the textual variant outperforms the flexible-interface executable variant in both gpt-5.5 settings. Simplification improves performance in three of the four model-effort settings, with the weakest setting as the only exception. The complete verification treatment ranks first in all four settings, although it uses substantially more resources. In the gpt-5.6-sol follow-up, the verification variant fully solves every public game at both reasoning efforts, achieves about 99% RHAE, and uses fewer than half the total actions of the human baseline. Because the model postdates these games and held-out performance remains untested, this result should be interpreted as saturation of the public set only.
2607.15439.paper_summary_zh: 我們之前的ARC-AGI-3代理捆綁了可執行的世界建模、計劃簡化和精確重播驗證，導致不清楚哪個想法對其性能負責。我們通過四個嵌套的基於Codex的代理來解決這個歸因問題：一個文本基準；一個沒有重播驗證的靈活介面可執行世界模型；相同的可執行模型與計劃簡化；以及一個固定介面的驗證處理，保留簡化並要求精確重現記錄的觀察結果。主要研究在公共ARC-AGI-3遊戲中，使用gpt-5.4和gpt-5.5以高和極高的推理努力評估所有四個代理。探索性後續研究使用gpt-5.6-sol以極高和最大推理努力評估文本和驗證變體。最穩健的結果是，每個代理變體在更強的模型和更大的推理努力下都有所改善。在每個模型努力設置中，變體之間的差異小於預期，而各個組件的效果在不同設置中有所不同。要求持久的可執行交付並不總是有利的：在gpt-5.5的兩個設置中，文本變體的表現超過了靈活介面的可執行變體。簡化在四個模型努力設置中的三個中改善了性能，唯一的例外是最弱的設置。完整的驗證處理在所有四個設置中排名第一，儘管它使用了大量的資源。在gpt-5.6-sol的後續研究中，驗證變體在兩個推理努力下完全解決了每個公共遊戲，達到了約99%的RHAE，並使用的總行動數不到人類基準的一半。由於該模型晚於這些遊戲，且保留的性能尚未測試，因此這一結果應被解釋為公共集的飽和。
